claim: For the complete isotropic Toupin–Mindlin gradient-elastic half-space, fix a tangential wavenumber \(\xi>0\) with a simple bulk-shear threshold \(k_0\) satisfying \(S(k_0)=\xi^2\), \(S'(k_0)>0\), and \(T(k_0)>0\), where \(S(k)=\sigma(k)^2\), \(T(k)=\tau(k)^2\), and \(\gamma_0=\sqrt{\xi^2+T(k_0)}\). As the nonzero signed coupling \(\alpha\to0\), the surface-wave decay exponent satisfies \(\beta=\frac{\xi^4}{\gamma_0^3}\alpha^2+O(\alpha^6)\), while its phase speed obeys \(V_{\mathrm{surf}}-V_{\mathrm{bulk}}=-\frac{c_s\xi^7}{\gamma_0^6S'(k_0)}\alpha^4+O(\alpha^8)\), where \(V_{\mathrm{bulk}}=c_sk_0/\xi\); thus localization is lost at quadratic order but the phase-speed gap closes at quartic order.
integrity: The exact arXiv v1 public date 2015-09-18 was verified; the journal record is dated 2015, but an exact earlier online-first day was not established from the inspected metadata.
The result is a local asymptotic derived from a published exact determinant; it is not an independent audit or a claim that the underlying dispersion relation is new.
scientific_limitations: Fixed positive tangential wavenumber and a simple bulk-shear threshold with S'(k0)>0 are required.
The asymptotic is local as the nonzero coupling tends to zero; it is not uniform near multiple thresholds or in a simultaneous wavenumber limit.
The full text of the 2019 comparison paper was not accessible; only its repository metadata and abstract were inspected.
title: Quartic Detachment at a Surface-Wave Existence Threshold
